topic: Steady State Multiplicity of Chemical Reactors, an Early Topic of Varma’s Interest. What Does It Say for Bioreactors?
title: Steady State Multiplicity of Chemical Reactors, an Early Topic of Varma’s Interest. What Does It Say for Bioreactors?
session_title: In Memory of Arvind Varma (Invited Talks)
abstract: Steady states and their potential multiplicity are of crucial interest to continuous chemical and bioreactors. Any activity in this area must accord recognition to Arvind Varma, who as a prized product of the Minnesota legacy, began his early career on this subject. Yet, it would seem that the context of bioreactors does not present a scenario so grossly at variance from that of chemical reactors as to merit a special narration in a session honoring my good friend Arvind. A strikingly distinct aspect of bioreactors, however, is the need to tangle with the complexity of large metabolic networks. Furthermore, the dynamic models required for this task must suitably recognize the role of metabolic regulation, a feature of the organism to navigate metabolism in specific ways as dictated by its gene network. The navigation is accomplished by preferred synthesis and activation of enzymes that catalyze specific reactions. While there is a substantial fraction of unknown regulatory features, even those that are known will add lavishly to the model complexity. This talk will present a commentary on how cybernetic models, which treat regulation as a survival motivated goal of the organism, confront the problem of steady state multiplicity and stability of bioreactors to make predictions that have been experimentally confirmed.

title: A Perspective on Engineering Catalysts
session_title: In Memory of Arvind Varma (Invited Talks)
abstract: Catalysts are used in a variety of processes to produce fuels, to make chemicals and materials, and to reduce pollution. These catalysts are developed within the context of a reactor that is then integrated into a process. The driving forces for developing and/or improving catalysts can include emerging opportunities, environmental regulations, sustainability, and competition. The catalyst developer plays a unique role in tailoring catalysts to cost-effectively meet reactor and process requirements. This tailoring or application development often is critical for establishing technical feasibility. The viability of the active site depends on the impact of inhibiting agents and poisons (contained in feed and recycle streams) on reaction rate. In addition to normal physical handling, the catalyst structure must withstand the reactor environment over its lifetime. Reactor design may depend on pressure drop considerations alone in one application or on downstream ease of separation in another. Input from subject matter experts in chemical and other engineering disciplines also may be needed. An incomplete understanding of catalyst deactivation under field conditions can pose a risk to process warranties. The risk profile for a process can increase further if corners are cut to compress the development timeline or if the process is scaled up without adequate piloting. An economic evaluation ultimately determines the fate of the technical work. This present talk will discuss select examples of application development from the author’s experience.

topic: Ozone for Facile C-H, C=C Activation in Emerging Feedstocks: Solvent and Reactor Engineering Aspects
title: Ozone for Facile C-H, C=C Activation in Emerging Feedstocks: Solvent and Reactor Engineering Aspects
session_title: In Memory of Arvind Varma (Invited Talks)
abstract: Ozone is a powerful oxidant that activates C=C and C-H bonds even at ambient temperatures. However, challenges related to safety and reaction selectivity have prevented ozone from being adopted widely in industry. This talk will highlight how these challenges can be addressed using appropriate solvents and reactors. Facile oxidation of emerging feedstocks (fatty acid methyl esters in vegetable oils, lignins and light alkanes) to value-added chemical precursors by ozone will be presented.

topic: Process Intensification and Modular Chemicals Production – Reaction Engineering Opportunities and Challenges
title: Process Intensification and Modular Chemicals Production – Reaction Engineering Opportunities and Challenges
session_title: In Memory of Arvind Varma (Invited Talks)
abstract: In honor of Arvind Varma, I will present our recent research at Texas A&M in collaboration with both the Texas A&M Energy Institute and the Mary Kay O’Connor Process Safety Center in the field of chemical reaction engineering for process intensification. Specifically, we will review efforts in design and development of manufacturable, modular microchannel reactors for energy applications, as well as efforts to integrate optimal control and inherently safer operation principles in the development of intensified reactor technologies for pharmaceutical and fine chemicals manufacture.
